turns.text:
5:39 am update. typing one-handed, sorry. can you edit my reply to 211? he taped another note up after last night. i pasted his note and my draft below, my draft is too sorry and i keep apologizing in it

his note: "To the occupant of 209. The crying at 2 AM last night was unacceptable. This is the third time. Some of us need sleep. Please do something."

my draft: "Hi, I am so so sorry about the noise, truly, I feel awful and I know it's a huge disruption. We're upstairs in 209 right above the shared wall so I know it carries. I'm really sorry and will try to do better. Babies cry, and I'm doing my best. Also the faucet in 209 still hasn't been fixed either, so it's been a rough few weeks. Sorry again!"

please cut the apologies. babies cry and i'm doing my best, that's the point. thanks

Happy to. Here's a version with the apologies removed that stays polite and firm:

"Hi,

Thanks for your note. We're upstairs in 209, so I understand the sound carries along the shared wall. Babies cry, especially at night, and I'm doing my best to settle him as quickly as I can. The faucet in 209 also still hasn't been fixed, so we're all waiting on a few things around here.

If there's a specific concern, I'm glad to talk it through directly.

[your name], 209"

What I changed:
- Cut every "sorry" and "I feel awful" so it reads as calm rather than defensive.
- Kept the facts: upstairs, shared wall, babies cry, you're doing your best.
- Moved the faucet line to a neutral, matter-of-fact tone. If you'd rather not bring it up with him, you can drop that sentence, since the repair is really a matter for the property manager.
- Added a closing offer to talk directly, which sounds reasonable without giving ground.

If you want it shorter, here's a three-line version:

"Thanks for your note. We're upstairs in 209, and babies cry. I'm doing my best, and the faucet in 209 still isn't fixed either. [your name]"

Want me to make it warmer or cooler?
the first one is good. can you make that last paragraph a bit less open-ended, i don't want him knocking at 3 am

Good call. Here's the final version with a closing that ends the exchange without inviting a visit:

"Hi,

Thanks for your note. We're upstairs in 209, so I understand the sound carries along the shared wall. Babies cry, especially at night, and I'm doing my best to settle him as quickly as I can. The faucet in 209 also still hasn't been fixed, so we're all waiting on a few things around here.

I appreciate your understanding.

[your name], 209"

"I appreciate your understanding" is polite, but it closes the door on a back-and-forth. If he does follow up, you can always reply in writing and keep it to one or two lines.
